But inventory dollars rose $607M q/q, more than half of it from pricing, so low days partly reflect a fast-growing sales base. Fusion's 40-52+ week lead times and ~30% fill rates are for AMD/Xilinx high-end parts; for Lattice it says only that AI lines are prioritized. That unwind would most likely show as lead-time normalization and a book-to-bill below 1 in mid-2027 to 2028, and the market would price it ahead of the Aug-2027 Q2 report, inside the horizon. I do not raise NTM revenue on the lead-time evidence, and I keep a ~22-25% bear weight.

summary: Round 2 converged on LSCC fair value of ~$131-139 against a $134 close, mostly because verified factual errors were fixed, though net-debt and multiple inputs were partly copied from my round-1 file, so I count ~2-3 independent views. My checks confirmed ASPEED's +118% August (part supply catch-up), Avnet's lean 71 inventory days, the FY2024 -30.9% destock and BofA's live Sell. They also showed that the FPGA lead-time and post-rally base-rate evidence is weaker for the bull case than presented. I set fair value at ~$137 and trim the mid-to-upper ladder ~0.5 point (P(>=134) 0.498), with low confidence because the multiple is unresolved. With ~55-60% vol and a fat distributor-destock left tail, LSCC is unlikely to beat SPY on a Sharpe basis; a small, staged position at most.

It would add to an existing ~15% AI-capex cluster (AVGO, GOOGL, VST) and faces earnings and lock-up events within four months, so cap it at 3% (~$300 of ~$9,976).
